queries.text: Lévi, Dogma and Ritual of High Magic (1855), translated from the author’s Portuguese, which uses the archaic "tu" (hence "thee/thy", as in How to Deal with Women) and "vós" in the woman’s words (rendered "you"). Bracketed insertions are the author’s. "LËVI" in the original corrected to "LÉVI". Compare Waite’s public-domain "Transcendental Magic" (1896).
"mulheres que amam demais" alludes to Robin Norwood’s "Women Who Love Too Much" (1985), whose established English title is used.
"phalus" kept as in the original (Latin-style spelling, italic); the standard spelling is "phallus".
"matrixianos" (the author’s coinage from the film The Matrix: men who live inside the conventional system without awareness) rendered "Matrixian". Alternatives: "Matrix-bound", "plugged-in".
